payload.measurement_basis: cgroup v2 memory.peak of the container's own scope, read via /proc/<pid>/cgroup, polled until exit; wall clock around docker run to exit; no --memory flag (measured usage, not behaviour under a cap)
scope_notes: Native amd64 only: x86 host, so the linux/amd64 platform path ran natively; the arm64-host-to-amd64-image emulation path was not exercised.
No artificial memory limit: docker run had no --memory flag; peak figures are measured usage, not behaviour under a cap.
payload.notes: Docker container measured run of the batch circuit. Companion to 006 (both circuits in one document) and 006a (solo), split one circuit per file at the maintainer's request. Built from the content-pinned image at commit dba5a975 and run via the documented verify.py entrypoint with --circuit selected at run time (batch default); all pinned input digests checked OK inside the container; the printed digest matched its canonical value. Batch container peak of ~11.05 GiB exceeds the ~8 GB previously estimated in the README.

scheme: EIP-191 personal_sign over the RFC8785/JCS canonicalization of the payload sub-object ONLY (json.dumps sort_keys, separators (',',':')); signing input = keccak256("\x19Ethereum Signed Message:\n" + str(jcs_len) + jcs_bytes), decimal-ASCII length; recover == signed_by (0x57fF0F084Cba33e6761503f90eEF0Da9F159350c). Authority: signers[signed_by] scope includes reproduction-attestations at https://x402.nsgoods.org/proof/index.json
